Folio for Agents 0.1

Everything has a place, and the place is the index.

Folio for Agents proposes where work, decisions and produced files live in a repository. Nothing is registered: putting a file where it belongs is the registration. The board is one reading of it.

Read the guideView source
$ curl -LsSf https://pguijas.github.io/folio/install.sh | sh

The format says where things go, so there is nothing to configure.

Each line below is a place, and what the place is for is written beside it. The counts are this board today.

Nothing is registered. Putting the file where it belongs is the registration.

A card's directory is read at build. Every regular file at its top level becomes an artifact on the card, name-sorted, and opens at a route. Six of these eighteen carry a label somebody wrote by hand. The other twelve are written down nowhere and are on the card anyway.

One card's trail, six sessions long, written by two tools across ten days.

The map's ## Trail row, opened on one card: one line per session. These six lines are unedited.

The build hands the store back as routes. Every one is plain text, and the size is what the server sent back.

Folio Docs 0.3.0 writes the first four for any site it builds: this site’s 131 pages as one index, the same 131 with their bodies attached, what the build accepts as data, and the Markdown each page was written from. The fifth is the optional adapter this site’s docs.yaml names, folio_agents.integrations.kanban, which republishes card directories byte for byte. This build carries eight of those directories and 67 files in them, because it publishes both of Folio’s boards.

You ask for it in plain English, and one line changes in one file.

There is no client library, no plugin and no API. An agent reads the protocol out of the repository and edits the card itself, so the Folio command is a convenience it can do without. Five ordinary asks, and the line each one leaves in a card file.

0.1 is the board. The rest is named, not built.

Folio's own agents board runs on 0.1 today. The three releases under it are named and scoped, and not built.
